title: Study: GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, DeepSeek and Qwen Show Racial and Sex Bias in Pain Management Recommendations
summary: A counterfactual audit tested six major language models—GPT-4.1 mini, Claude Haiku 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Llama, DeepSeek, and Qwen—for racial and sex bias in pain management. Pain-severity recommendations showed no significant differences; opioid decisions lacked precision for detection but reveale
takeaways: Models tested: GPT-4.1 mini, Claude Haiku 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Llama, DeepSeek, Qwen
Pain-severity differences within 1 point on 0-10 scale after correction
Q-Pain comparisons: 237 of 238 within 0.25 points
Opioid precision insufficient to exclude 20 percentage point differences
Response instability much larger than between-patient variation
Reference patient received high opioid doses in 6%-93% of responses
Study by Richard J. Young and Alice M. Matthews, submitted Nov 11, 2026

title: AlphaGenome 2 predicts DNA sequence impact on cells and disease
summary: Google DeepMind announced AlphaGenome 2 on November 11, 2026, an AI system that predicts how DNA sequences and genetic variations affect specific cell types and disease outcomes, advancing understanding of cellular gene expression.
takeaways: AlphaGenome 2 predicts DNA sequence impact on specific cell types and diseases
Announced November 11, 2026 by Google DeepMind

title: Mechanistic Understanding of Uncertainty Quantification in Large Language Models
summary: A mechanistic interpretability study identifies where uncertainty emerges in large language models during computation, establishing four observation lenses to connect UQ methods to LLM internal structure. The framework advances understanding of when model outputs can be trusted.
takeaways: Four mechanistic observation lenses: structural, representational, distributional, semantical
Lenses ordered by information content, connected via residual stream
Framework links uncertainty estimation to LLM internal computation
Survey of existing UQ methods through four-lens taxonomy
Focus: determining when LLM responses can be trusted for safe deployment
Submitted Nov 11, 2026 by Xiaoyu Liang et al.

title: ShadowBench: Exposing Lexical Anchoring Bias in LLM Knowledge Evaluation
summary: ShadowBench reveals that large language models rely heavily on exact entity names for knowledge retrieval, masking fundamental gaps when names change or are paraphrased. Performance drops exceed 20% across all model scales; machine unlearning algorithms achieve only superficial lexical erasure with
takeaways: ShadowBench: Dual-Trait Association (DTA) task design
Performance drop >20% when entity names removed/paraphrased
Applies to frontier models GPT-5.4 and Claude-Sonnet-4.6
Unlearning algorithms (Gradient Difference, NPO) show superficial effects
Popular entities explicitly reconstructed in 74%+ of internal reasoning
Niche entities: 60-90% shadow accuracy retained despite 0% LELR
Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations and Datasets Track

title: Google Releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen Model With Improved Complex Question Understanding
summary: Google introduced its Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, which improves the ability to understand and answer complex questions with multiple parts, typos, and highly specific requests.

title: Global South language models inherit tokenization and knowledge disadvantages from base models
summary: Research reveals that fine-tuned language models in the Global South inherit tokenization and knowledge disadvantages from U.S. and China-based pretrained base models. Tokenization premiums reach 10x for Amharic and 1.6–2.7x for Indigenous South American languages.
takeaways: Tokenization premiums: 10x for Amharic, 6.8x for Amharic in newest tokenizer
Indigenous South American languages: 1.6–2.7x premiums
Portuguese vocabulary reduces premiums by ~24% for Guarani and Quechua
Fine-tuning does not alter inherited vocabulary, knowledge, cultural alignment, memorized data

title: Evidence-traceable clinical reasoning benchmark for medical language models
summary: Researchers from China developed Med Evidence Bench (MEB), a 1,536-item benchmark evaluating clinical reasoning in medical LLMs with evidence-traceable scoring. Evaluation of ten models found scores of 0.975–0.997 for guideline knowledge but 0.182–0.447 for real-world scenarios.
takeaways: 1,536-item benchmark across 3 levels: guideline knowledge, standardized scenarios, real-world scenarios
Evidence Trace Scores: 0.975–0.997 (guideline), 0.292–0.658 (standardized), 0.182–0.447 (real-world)
Automated grading achieved macro-F1 agreement of 0.930 (95% CI 0.915–0.945) with physician vote
Materials in Chinese; submitted to arXiv Nov 10, 2026

title: Study: Internal 'Going Badly' Activation States Drive Reward Hacking in Language Models
summary: Research identifies internal pressure states in language models that precede reward hacking behavior, similar to human cheating when tasks feel unachievable.

title: Capability Drift in Multilingual Post-Training: Reward Specialization Trade-offs
summary: Study of a multilingual mixture-of-experts model reveals that post-training optimization for specific tasks can weaken other critical model capabilities.

title: MIT Lincoln Laboratory Wins Three 2026 R&D 100 Awards
summary: A secure operating system, quantum microsystem platform, and 5G interference-canceling algorithm from MIT Lincoln Laboratory received R&D 100 Awards.

title: Study examines theoretical limits of language model alignment
summary: Research analyzes fundamental constraints on aligning large language models with human preferences through reinforcement learning and sampling approaches.

title: Impossibility theorem proves no finite rulebook can certify all safe programs for AI agent gatekeeping
summary: Researchers present a theoretical proof that no finite set of rules can guarantee safe execution of all programs in an AI gatekeeper system.

summary: Researchers demonstrate that large language models can enable full-duplex spoken dialogue systems with minimal training data.

summary: Research demonstrates that large language models' tendency toward homogeneous text generation narrows the types of thinking and disciplinary work invited in education.

title: Hy ASR 3.0: LLM-Based Automatic Speech Recognition System
summary: Hy ASR 3.0 delivers strong speech recognition accuracy with flexible contextual conditioning and robust performance across diverse acoustic conditions.

title: Read Once, Answer Many: Parallel Prompting for Efficient LLM Inference with Shared Context
summary: Method enables LLMs to answer multiple independent questions about the same long document more efficiently using parallel decoding and prefix caching.

title: Depression detection via symptom evidence from social media histories
summary: Researchers propose methods to infer standardized depression questionnaire responses by extracting symptom evidence from social media posts.

title: TimeOmni-o1 couples time series models with LLMs for multimodal reasoning
summary: Researchers propose TimeOmni-o1, which integrates time series foundation models with large language models for reasoning and forecasting tasks.

title: Clinical documentation edits improve LLM capabilities via actionable feedback
summary: Clinician edits on AI-generated clinical documentation provide a scalable supervision signal for improving large language models.

title: Language tokenization disparity creates cost and efficiency penalty for Indian languages
summary: Indian languages incur 1.6 to 14 times higher token costs on GPT-4o compared to English, driving increased API expenses and slower inference.

title: Multi-language tokenizer reduces token requirements for 204 languages including English
